on 4 November, 2025
 The Honourable Smt.Justice Tirumala Devi Eada
 Criminal Petition No.13530 of 2025
Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioner-accused seeking to quash the proceedings in SC No.447 of 2023 on the file of the District and Sessions Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B. Nagar,
for the offences under Sections 376, 420, 417 and 506 IPC.

entities.text: District and Sessions Judge, Ranga Reddy District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri KVN Prasad, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Jithender Rao Veeramalla,
learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent No.1-State.
3.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the de facto complainant is a married woman and that the allegation that the petitioner has committed rape on her is utterly false.

He further submitted that both the petitioner and the respondent No.2 are advocates and that since she is a married woman the petitioner never entertained any relationship with her and has also not promised anything to her and never deceived in any manner.

He further submitted that there is a huge delay in lodging the complaint and the alleged offence is shown to have occurred on 05.05.2022 and the complaint is lodged on 03.10.2022 and the delay is not explained.
Therefore, he prayed to quash the proceedings.
ETD,J 4.

The learned Additional Public Prosecutor has submitted that in the first instance, the petitioner was given a cool drink and when she was in subconscious stage, rape was committed on her and later on, she was being blackmailed and the physical abuse got continued.
He further submitted that though she is a married woman she is divorced and is single and was staying with her daughter at her parent's place.
He further submitted that the prosecution could collect ample evidence to prove the offence against the petitioner and hence, he prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. Perused the record.
6.

The contents of the complaint point out that the de facto complainant was offered a cool drink,
pursuant to which she was in semi-conscious stage and that she was taken to a secluded area at Moinabad and has committed rape on her.
Subsequently, she was being lured with a promise that he would marry her.
Inspite of her marital status, he expressed interest on marrying her.
The petitioner continued the physical relationship, but when she asked him to marry her, he started evading her and has threatened her and her family members with dire consequences.
Thus, the prime facie allegations point out the offences against the petitioner.
The statements of the witnesses and the truth or otherwise in the ETD,J allegations need to be tested during the course of trial.
Though the learned counsel for the petitioner pleaded that there is delay in lodging the complaint, the same cannot be a ground to quash the proceedings.

Thus, it is not proper to quash the proceedings against Dasari Anil Kumar, vs State Of Telangana, on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69093721/
1 the petitioner at this stage.

sentences.text: Hence, it is deemed appropriate to dispense with the attendance of the petitioner before the trial court.

7. Accordingly, the criminal petition is disposed of dispensing with the attendance of the petitioner before the trial court provided he is represented by a counsel on every date of hearing before the trial court and he shall appear before the trial court as and when his presence is required.
Miscellaneous Petitions, if any pending, shall stand closed.
